request.spec: The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The people, claims and pools exports taken while an as-of date is set use the as-of figures.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The people, claims and pools exports now use the as-of figures while an as-of date is set. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests; before the fix the main "as of exports" test failed.

**What was wrong:** the server already answers every read with the as-of figures when an as-of date is set. But the people and claims exports were built from data the screen had already loaded, and that data isn't stored separately per date. So an export taken right after setting the date still showed the current figures: Ada's due came out as 2.00 instead of 1.00, and Ben showed a retirement date he didn't have yet on that date.

**The fix (front end only):**
- I added `features/export/fresh.ts`, a small helper that re-reads parts of the sheet from the store. Each read carries the as-of date when one is set and updates the screen's copy of that data.
- `ExportPeople` and `ExportClaims` now re-read the sheet's today, people, claims, rates and settings (and periods, for claims) when the button is pressed, then build the CSV from that data.
- `ExportPools` already re-read the pools; it now uses the same helper.

No stored data, server code or `data-testid` values changed, and nothing new is written to the audit file.
